chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from Ibrahim ibn Muhraz al-Khas'ami from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him about a girl with whom a man enjoys temporary marriage (mut'ah). He said, 'Yes, unless she is a young girl who is deceived.' I said, 'May God perfect you, what is the limit/age at which, when she reaches it, she is not deceived?' He said, 'A daughter of ten years (of age).'

And among the reasons for this narration is that the report may have been issued in the context of precautionary dissimulation (taqiyyah). And that which indicates this is what was narrated: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Fadl ibn Kathir al-Mada'ini from al-Muhallab al-Dallal, that he wrote to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A woman was with me in the house, then she married herself to me and made God and His angels witness to that. Then her father married her to another man. What do you say?' He (peace be upon him) wrote back, 'Permanent marriage is not valid except with a guardian and two witnesses, and temporary marriage (mut'ah) can be with a virgin. Conceal it from yourself, may God have mercy on you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the age limit for a girl in temporary marriage and how does taqiyya apply?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the age of maturity for temporary marriage (mut'ah) at ten years, distinguishing when a girl is no longer considered 'deceived' (ghurrah) by her guardian. It further clarifies the procedural differences between permanent and temporary unions, noting that while permanent marriage requires a guardian and witnesses, mut'ah with a virgin can be conducted privately, a ruling often linked to taqiyya to avoid public scrutiny of the practice.
